networkShareDefinition: (bcadCurrencyCheck + bcadDivergenceFetch + layer23SetbackProbe + layer23SetbackBuild) / wallMsTotal * 100 — all live outbound HTTP to ArcGIS endpoints
dbQueryShareDefinition: (situsQuery + alreadyPromotedQuery + geomResolve + boundaryEdgesRead) / wallMsTotal * 100 — Neon round-trips
allIoShareDefinition: every named bucket except otherCompute and warmThenVerify... measured as bucketSum/wallMsTotal, i.e. 100 minus otherCompute; warmThenVerify is compute on the dry leg and is included in the geometry share below
geometryComputeShareDefinition: (warmThenVerify + otherCompute) / wallMsTotal * 100 — all in-process geometry/verify work on the dry leg
liveHttpCallsPerParcelNote: 1 BCAD parcel-currency call + 1 layer-23 setback probe on every parcel, plus a second layer-23 call on the ~22% of parcels that clear the probe and reach the descriptor build. Both layer-23 calls are the identical uncached query.
finding: Network and DB I/O dominate: 97.4 percent of parcel-loop wall time is blocking I/O and only 8.89 percent is geometry compute. Live ArcGIS HTTP is 53.29 percent of wall (BCAD parcel-currency 27.15 percent at 1.0 calls/parcel, plus Bastrop layer-23 setback lookups 26.14 percent at 1.20 calls/parcel), and Neon DB round-trips are another 37.81 percent, dominated by the per-parcel situs_address query at 27.84 percent. The planner's hypothesis is confirmed in direction but incomplete in scope: BCAD alone is only about a quarter of the cost, and three other per-parcel serial round-trips (situs query at ~92 ms, layer-23 setback probe at ~80 ms, already-promoted check at ~91 ms) each cost about as much as the BCAD call. Every one of these is a single-parcel serial round-trip at roughly 80 to 92 ms, so the pipeline is latency-bound, not compute-bound, and the fix shape is batching plus caching plus concurrency, not geometry optimization. Two specific free wins found in the code: the layer-23 setback record is fetched TWICE per qualifying parcel with identical arguments and no cache (districtHasPerParcelSetbackRow at ~line 553 then buildBastropPerParcelSetbackDescriptor at ~line 570), and the situs_address query is a per-parcel single-row SELECT against txgio_parcel that could be one batched prefetch for the whole cohort. Note two buckets read zero on this dry leg and will add cost on an apply leg: boundaryEdgesRead (guarded by !dryRun) and bcadDivergenceFetch (fires under --force-repromote or an edge-count mismatch), so a --force-overwrite apply will be slower per parcel than the 330 ms measured here.
caveats: Dry-run only. No apply-path costs measured: promoteDepthWarmToStorage write-then-verify, promoteHonestVerifyDecline writes, and boundaryEdgesRead all add per-parcel atoms-DB round-trips on an apply leg.

This run is a --city-cohort dry leg without --force-overwrite, so 390 of 500 parcels exited early at the no-setback-row branch (before geomResolve/warmThenVerify). That is why geomResolve fired 63 times and warmThenVerify 53 times against 500 parcels processed. Deep-path parcels cost more per parcel (P50 644 ms, P95 1081 ms) than the 330 ms all-parcel mean.

The master planner's 522 ms/parcel figure (3,021,150 ms / 5,785 parcels) is a whole-script number including setup; the comparable figure here is 330 ms/parcel loop-only or 387 ms/parcel including the 28.3 s setup. Same order of magnitude, and the bucket shares are the load-bearing result, not the absolute mean.

Single-sample run per limit. A limit=200 pre-run produced consistent per-call means (situsQuery 91.9 ms, bcadCurrencyCheck 91.0 ms, layer23SetbackProbe 92.0 ms), so the per-call latencies are stable across runs.
